messages:
maya: Alert from monitoring — while triaging a support case I found a Sentry attachment that contains what looks like a service API key (starts with rk_live_...).

kyle: Which attachment name? I'll grab it from the ticket.

maya: attachment: error_trace_2026-03-20.zip (Zendesk ticket #3425).

kyle: pulling now. If it's a live key we should revoke and block immediately. @alex can you run a quick usage lookup?

alex: running a query against token-usage logs: `select count(*) from api_logs where token like 'rk_live_%' and timestamp > now() - interval '24 hours'` — preliminary: 432 requests from 3 distinct IPs.

jordan: any customer IDs tied to those requests?

alex: two tenant ids seen: cust_998 and cust_102 — most responses were 401/403 but I see ~12 200s to the embeddings endpoint. diving deeper.

maya: Containment plan (short):
1) revoke the exposed token
2) apply temporary deny RBAC policy to any principals referencing it
3) rotate KMS-wrapped secrets if token material is derived from CMK
4) search S3 / support attachments / sentry exports for other occurrences
5) prepare comms if customers were affected

sam: For comms: if only internal service token was used, internal note suffices. If any successful calls touched customer data we need to notify.

alex: Revoked via admin CLI: `ri-admin revoke-token --token rk_live_ABC123 --reason "leaked in support attachment"` — API returned 204. Also applied temporary deny-role to svc principals referencing that token.

audit-bot: Created ticket SEC-2026-031 for investigation & impact analysis. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-2026-031

maya: Good. Next search: `aws s3api list-objects --bucket support-attachments --query "Contents[?contains(Key, 'error_trace')].Key" | xargs -I {} aws s3 cp s3://support-attachments/{} - | grep -E "rk_live_[A-Za-z0-9]{6,}"` — I'll run this across buckets and zendesk exports.

kyle: On KMS: if the token was derived from KMS-protected secret we need to re-encrypt with a new CMK. @alex check which key is used by svc-ingest.

alex: svc-ingest uses KMS key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:key/abcd-efgh. Rotation is yearly. I'll create a new CMK, re-encrypt affected secrets and rotate. Starting re-encryption now.

jordan: Audit logs show the token was created by the deploy pipeline on 2025-12-01 and last used ~72 hours ago. No privilege escalations in those successful calls. Suggest: rotate, run customer smoke tests, schedule postmortem.

maya: Owners: alex = revoke+rotate+re-encrypt, kyle = search attachments & S3, jordan = audit + smoke tests, sam = comms draft. ETA for initial impact report: 2 hours.

sam: I'll draft an internal blameless note and a customer template. Share tenant ids and affected API surfaces once confirmed.

maya: Update in 30m please. Thanks :thumbsup: 

rotbot: deploybot: infra-rule update applied — deny role `support-attachment-access` added to service principals pending investigation.

maya: Added forensic retention: saving all artifacts, handing off to forensics if we see exfil patterns. We'll include remediation & follow-ups in the postmortem.

alex: Quick note: no further successful calls after revoke. Running re-encrypt job now, will post job id in ticket.

kyle: Found two more attachments with same pattern, quarantining them and creating internal copies for analysis.

jordan: Smoke tests for cust_998 and cust_102 running — initial results show no data leakage beyond API request/response metadata. Will confirm.

maya: Great work. Keep updates in SEC-2026-031 thread. We'll schedule a 1-hour postmortem tomorrow to cover root cause (support bundle scrub policy), RBAC gaps, and KMS rotation cadence.
